extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in freethought, secularism, and the political/moral defence of atheists (19th-century England)
extracted.subtask_description: A short lecture/essay arguing for the moral rectitude and legal equality of affirmative Atheism (Cosmism/Secularism) and prescribing the acceptable limits and conduct for its advocates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positivism in Principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Affirmative Atheism (Cosmism) must be grounded in a positive realism of Nature rather than mere negation; negative critique should be complemented by constructive, positive principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirmative Atheism asserts the self-existence, self-action, self-subsistence, eternity, and infinity of the universe and supplies positive moral and practical aims ("teach that nature is the Bible of truth, work is worship"). Mere negative Atheism (pure negation) is criticised as leaving the mind 'untenanted' and may be guilty of neglecting to supply a wholesome moral and social alternative (compared to leaving ground bare after pulling up weeds). Practical objectives and the substitution of science and moral criteria for superstition are required; avoid "reckless iconoclasticism."

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness in Profession of Opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocates must practise scientific reservation and linguistic exactness: confess ignorance where appropriate, understate claims, and avoid misleading or libellous terminology (prefer 'Cosmism' or 'Secularism' to 'Atheism' when those terms better convey the position).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The logic of Affirmative Atheism begins in self-confession: 'not to say that you do see when you do not' and to keep within facts and proof. Exactness of phraseology is 'well understood self-defence.' Avoid conflating attributes with existence (e.g., saying 'God is Light' confuses attribute with existence). Suffer not an opponent to choose names for you: banish the unqualified term 'Atheism' which libels and prefer 'Cosmism' or 'Secularism.' Cultivate modesty of pretension and scientific reservation; understate cases and keep to what can be proved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispassionateness in Judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain an open, patient, non-dogmatic mind and a dispassionate, respectful tone in speech and advocacy; reject invective, denunciation, and intolerance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dogmatism and passion imperil truth; Cosmist temperament should be reachable by reason and not impatient with dissent. Opinion in a minority should not resort to invective; maintain respectfulness and fairness of speech to placate opposition and avoid inflaming prejudice. The force of truth lies in 'invincible patience' and 'invincible perseverance of exposition.' Examples and admonitions appear through the text: reason with superstition, avoid shutting eyes and ears to opposing arguments, and keep advocacy on 'the high places of dispassionate advocacy.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanism in Conception (Reliance of Humanity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a standard of value within humanity rather than depending on an external supernatural standard; rely on human self-regulation, responsibility, and the moral dignity of secular life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a standard within the universe—'I choose humanity.' Avoid hardness, assumption, egotism, insubordination to worth, and irreverence. Show that nature and humanity contain elements of self-sustainment and self-regulation; vindicate that left to nature, philosophy, reputation and law, reliable rationality and moral conduct arise. Practical examples and appeals: civic improvement, moral service, and the dignity of work. The conception implies temperate reverence and humility before facts (e.g., reflections on suffering, the future life, and the moral duties of service and endurance).
